 Arab Weather - Computer simulation maps at the Arab Weather Center indicate that northern Levant will be affected by a winter low-pressure system, following the strong atmospheric instability that affected the region during the past few days, as the low-pressure system is expected to bring heavy rains and a noticeable drop in temperatures.
 This low-pressure system is also expected to bring the first chance of snowfall over the high mountain peaks in Lebanon during the current season, given the winter weather that will accompany its impact on the region.
 A winter low-pressure system will affect Syria and Lebanon on Thursday and Friday. 
 God willing, Syria and Lebanon will be affected on Thursday and Friday by a winter low-pressure system, accompanied by a highly effective cold front moving towards the region. Temperatures will drop on Thursday and rain will fall, especially on the coasts. Then the rainy front will cross on Thursday evening and night/Friday, with heavy to very heavy rain falling on large areas of western Syria and Lebanon.
 The heaviest rainfall is concentrated particularly on the Syrian coastal areas, including Latakia, Tartus and the surrounding areas, as well as the Lebanese coast, especially Tripoli and the areas north of Beirut. Rainfall is expected to extend to the interior regions, including large parts of Lebanon and several Syrian governorates, including Homs, Hama, Idlib and Raqqa.
 These rainfalls are accompanied by cold weather, active winds and sometimes strong gusts, along with a clear drop in temperatures. The weather disturbance is expected to cause high waves and disruption to maritime navigation, with the possibility of waterspouts forming off the Syrian and Lebanese coasts.
 Heavy rains and warnings of flash floods and rising water levels 
 The low-pressure system is expected to bring large amounts of rain to large parts of Syria and Lebanon, especially coastal areas, where heavy and continuous rainfall may lead to flash floods, overflowing valleys and streams, and possibly local flooding and a significant rise in water levels in low-lying areas.
 These weather conditions call for attention to the dangers of crossing valleys and torrents, especially in areas that experience heavy rainfall over a short period of time.
 First chance of snowfall on the high mountain peaks of Lebanon 
 The low-pressure system is expected to provide the first opportunity of the current season for snowfall over the high mountain peaks in Lebanon, coinciding with a drop in temperatures and the rush of the cold air mass accompanying the low-pressure system.
 Jordan and Palestine are under the influence of colder than usual air masses. 
 In Jordan and Palestine, forecasts indicate that the region will be affected by the consequences of colder-than-usual air masses moving towards the Levant, leading to a gradual decrease in temperatures on Thursday, with this decrease expected to increase on Friday.
 The Kingdom and Palestine are expected to be under the influence of what is called the jet stream in the upper layers of the atmosphere, which prevents the penetration of the low-pressure system and its direct effects towards the south. However, it is not unlikely that there will be an opportunity on Friday for some local rain to fall on parts of Palestine and Jordan, coinciding with the region continuing to be affected by colder than usual weather.
 And God knows best.
